name: First Light Basin

stars.name: First Light
stars.notes: A calm, slightly aged yellow star with steady output and a clean spectrum; survey teams call it the quietest sky on the Shelf, which is why the listening posts are here.

planets.name: Kindling
planets.notes: A sun-baked cinder used only as a navigation marker; its orbit is the inner boundary of the Basin's protected science zone.

planets.name: Vantage
planets.notes: A rust-colored desert world with thin air and perfect seeing conditions; automated observatories dot its highlands, watching the sky without a single human present.

planets.name: Basin
planets.notes: A temperate world of grass plains and shallow seas hosting the First Contact Enclave: two million researchers, linguists, and settlers living under the strictest communication protocols in charted space.

planets.name: Shallows
planets.notes: A warm ocean world teeming with simple native life; landing is prohibited and every probe that descends is sterilized twice and never returns.

planets.name: Ledgerworld
planets.notes: A banded pale giant whose moons carry the system's fuel infrastructure; skimming operations run under charter so the refinery traffic never crosses the science lanes.

planets.name: Far Harbor
planets.notes: A frozen outer world with a single Guild beacon; ships bound rimward top off here before the long dark.

anomalies.name: The Greeting
anomalies.notes: A structured, repeating emission from empty space that answers no transmission but pauses, precisely, whenever Basin's largest radio telescope transmits. It has done so for eleven years. No one has decoded it; no one has stopped listening.

stations.name: Enclave Ring
stations.notes: The administrative and quarantine hub above Basin; every arrival passes through three days of decontamination and one hour of protocol briefing before descent.

stations.name: Listening Post Nine
stations.notes: The array station nearest the Greeting's source; its crew serves two-year silent rotations and is famously superstitious about saying anything aloud near the antennas.

faction_control.notes: A joint academic-charter authority governs the system with a single law: nothing that originates here may be transmitted outward without unanimous review. Trade exists at the edges; curiosity runs the center.

history: Basin was chartered as a research preserve after Shallows' native biosphere was confirmed, making it the first system in the Shelf where settlement was deliberately subordinated to study.
Eleven years ago Listening Post Nine recorded the first Greeting pulse, and overnight the system changed from a quiet preserve to the most protected address in charted space.
Three years ago a smuggler tried to sell recordings of the signal coreward; the Enclave's pursuit board caught him in the Far Harbor lanes, and his ship is still held in quarantine as evidence.
description: A single steady yellow sun shines over six clean orbits, and the worlds beneath it look arranged rather than found: a desert of perfect telescopic silence, a temperate plain-world, an ocean that seethes with uncontacted life. From orbit, Basin's continents show the low silver geometry of the Enclave's cities, small against the grass, as if the planet were mostly holding its breath.

Two million people live under the Concord's protocols, most of them scientists, all of them volunteers who passed years of screening to be here. Traffic is light and deliberate: supply runners to Ledgerworld's refineries, sterilized probes down to Shallows, and the constant patient attention of Listening Post Nine aimed at the outer dark. Everyone in the system knows exactly why they are allowed to stay.

Because something out past Far Harbor says hello. The Greeting repeats on a schedule that has never slipped, pauses when addressed, and ignores every attempt at conversation beyond that single courtesy. The Enclave's linguists have built careers on its structure; its theologians have built schisms. The one rule everyone agrees on: whatever it is, humanity gets one first impression, and it has not been made yet.
